output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: ResourcesServiceImpl builds `fullName = currentDir + "/" + name` (createDirectory line 140, createResource line 217, onlineCreateResource line 973) and passes it to HadoopUtils, which turns it into a Hadoop `Path` (HadoopUtils.java lines ~279-312). `name`/`fileName` were checked with `FileUtils.directoryTraversal(String)` in these methods, but `currentDir` never was; `onlineCreateResource` additionally never checked `fileSuffix` for traversal even though it gets embedded into `name` before the fullName concatenation (e.g. fileSuffix='../../x' would bypass the fileName-only check).

Fix:
1. Added `FileUtils.directoryTraversal(String[] pathSegments)` in dolphinscheduler-common's FileUtils - splits an existing check (`directoryTraversal(String)`, which flags any '/' or canonical-vs-absolute mismatch e.g. '..') across path segments, so a legitimate multi-level directory like '/aa/bb' passes while '/aa/../../etc' is rejected. This reuses the existing, already-tested traversal-detection primitive instead of introducing new logic.
2. In ResourcesServiceImpl: createDirectory (line 136) now also checks `currentDir.split("/")`; createResource now checks `currentDir.split("/")` right after verifyFile and before the fullName is built/used; onlineCreateResource now checks `fileSuffix.trim()` and `currentDir.split("/")` alongside the existing `fileName` check, before any of those values are folded into `fullName`/`name`.
3. Added regression tests: FileUtilsTest.testDirectoryTraversalOnPathSegments (unit tests for the new overload, positive and negative cases) and three new assertions in ResourcesServiceTest (createResource, createDirectory, onlineCreateResource) that stub the new overload to return true for a malicious `currentDir` ('/../../etc') and assert the service returns VERIFY_PARAMETER_NAME_FAILED instead of proceeding to the HDFS write.

updateResource was not touched - it has no `currentDir` parameter; its `fullName` is derived from the already-persisted `originFullName` plus `name`, and `name` is already validated via `verifyFile` before any HDFS operation, so it was not part of the vulnerable data flow.
output_json.risk_notes:
Behavioral risk is low: the new check only rejects `currentDir` values containing a literal '..' (or single-dot) path segment, which is never a legitimate resource-center directory path; ordinary nested paths like '/a/b/c' are unaffected (verified in FileUtilsTest). All 16 existing + new ResourcesServiceTest cases pass, and a full multi-module `mvn package` (skipping tests) compiles cleanly.

Sandbox testing caveat: this Docker image's dolphinscheduler-api test classpath includes junit-jupiter (pulled in transitively) without junit-vintage-engine, so Maven Surefire's auto-selected JUnit-Platform provider silently discovers 0 of the ~69 JUnit4/PowerMock test classes when running `mvn test` on dolphinscheduler-api as-is (confirmed this occurs identically on the unmodified baseline via `git stash`, so it's a pre-existing environment gap, not something this patch introduces). To get a real pass/fail signal for ResourcesServiceTest I temporarily added a `junit-vintage-engine` test-scope dependency to dolphinscheduler-api/pom.xml, ran the tests (16/16 passed, including the 3 new traversal-rejection assertions), and then reverted that pom.xml change since it isn't part of the security fix (confirmed via `git diff` that pom.xml is no longer modified). The regression_commands above reflect commands that work reliably in this environment (FileUtilsTest, which runs cleanly without the vintage-engine workaround, plus a full package build); running dolphinscheduler-api's JUnit4 suite in CI/a properly configured environment (or with junit-vintage-engine present) should show ResourcesServiceTest passing 16/16 as verified locally.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-22 path traversal in the resource-center: `currentDir` (and, in the online-create path, `fileSuffix`) were concatenated into `fullName` and passed down to HadoopUtils' `new Path(...)` calls without ever being checked for traversal sequences, even though the sibling `name`/`fileName` parameter usually was. Added a directory-aware traversal check (`FileUtils.directoryTraversal(String[])`) and applied it to all three request entry points that build `fullName` from an attacker-supplied `currentDir`: createDirectory, createResource, and onlineCreateResource (which also validates fileSuffix, since it gets spliced into the resource name before the same construction). This blocks the create/update/online-create paths described in the alert (and copy/rename, since those reuse the same fullName) without touching HDFS-layer code.
